title: A Square-Root Budget
statement:
Let $x,y,z$ be positive real numbers with $\sqrt x+\sqrt y+\sqrt z=1$. Prove that
$$\frac{x^2+yz}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}+\frac{y^2+zx}{\sqrt{2y^2(z+x)}}+\frac{z^2+xy}{\sqrt{2z^2(x+y)}}\ge1.$$
hints: Split each numerator: $\frac{x^2+yz}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}=\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}+\frac{yz}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}$, and apply Cauchy-Schwarz to each sum against $\sum\sqrt{2(y+z)}$.
After both applications it is enough to show $2\sum\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}\ge\sum\sqrt{2(y+z)}$. Note $\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}=z$.
solution:
Write $T=\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}$ and $R=\sqrt{2(y+z)}+\sqrt{2(z+x)}+\sqrt{2(x+y)}$, and let $L$ be the left-hand side.

By Cauchy-Schwarz,
$$\left(\sum\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}\right)R\ge\left(\sqrt x+\sqrt y+\sqrt z\right)^2=1$$
and
$$\left(\sum\frac{yz}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}\right)R\ge T^2.$$
Adding,
$$L\cdot R\ge1+T^2\ge2T.$$
So it suffices to prove $2T\ge R$.

By AM-GM,
$$\left[\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\left(\frac12\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}\right)\right]^2\ge4\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}\left(\frac12\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}\right)=2(y+z),$$
that is,
$$\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}\ge\sqrt{2(y+z)}.$$
Similarly
$$\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}\ge\sqrt{2(z+x)},\qquad \sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}\ge\sqrt{2(x+y)}.$$
Adding the three gives $2T\ge R$, so $L\ge1$. $\blacksquare$

rubric.criterion: Applies Cauchy-Schwarz to get $\left(\sum\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{2x^2(y+z)}}\right)\sum\sqrt{2(y+z)}\ge(\sqrt x+\sqrt y+\sqrt z)^2=1$, or an equivalent bound that uses the condition.

Applies Cauchy-Schwarz to the $yz$ parts and combines, reducing the problem to $2\sum\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}\ge\sum\sqrt{2(y+z)}$ (for example via $1+T^2\ge2T$), or an equivalent reduction. Award 1 for the second Cauchy-Schwarz alone.
Proves $\sqrt{\frac{yz}{x}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{zx}{y}}+\frac12\sqrt{\frac{xy}{z}}\ge\sqrt{2(y+z)}$ (for example by AM-GM), or an equivalent estimate for one term.
Adds the three cyclic estimates to obtain $2T\ge R$ and concludes. A complete proof by another route earns all marks.

fatal_errors.error: Uses the condition as $x+y+z=1$ instead of $\sqrt x+\sqrt y+\sqrt z=1$.
Applies an inequality in the wrong direction, such as an upper bound where a lower bound is needed, so that the chain does not prove the claim.
Proves the inequality only for $x=y=z$ or another special case.
